enterprises.text: For enterprises Your expertise. A standard your agent can learn from. Build around the work your business actually does. We help define the tasks, evaluations and training materials that make your standard of quality explicit. Discuss your workflow What an engagement includes Start where the work gets difficult An agent can produce a plausible answer and still miss the detail that matters. A policy exception. A missing source. An action that should wait for review. These are useful starting points for an evaluation and training project. A focused engagement A clear question. A concrete handoff. The scope begins with one workflow and the evidence needed to judge it. 01 / Define Agree on the standard. Map the task, available tools, acceptable outputs and failures that matter. Identify the domain experts who can review the criteria. Handoff: workflow brief and acceptance criteria. 02 / Make Build the material. Shape a scoped evaluation set, reviewed examples or a repeatable environment. Record where each task comes from and how it should be assessed. Handoff: versioned tasks, rubrics and supporting artifacts. 03 / Examine Find the useful signal. Apply the agreed checks to agent attempts. Separate objective failures from expert preferences and surface disagreements for review. Handoff: an assessment of failures and a prioritized revision plan. 04 / Refine Make the next iteration testable. Use the findings to guide training material or environment changes. Define a held-out evaluation before comparing iterations. Handoff: an agreed next experiment and evidence to compare it. How we partner Close to the work. Built around your team. 01 / Embedded Work at the same table. We shape the evaluation, tasks and feedback alongside your engineers and domain experts. Your team stays close to the decisions that define quality. For teams building their own training loop. Explore an embedded project ↗ 02 / Managed A defined body of work. Agree on the workflow, acceptance criteria and handoff. We scope the task set, evaluation materials or environment work, with review points along the way. For teams that need a focused deliverable. Scope a managed project ↗ Before work begins Get the boundaries right, together. Each engagement needs an explicit agreement on permitted data, access, retention, ownership and acceptance. These decisions belong in the scope. Data & permission Identify what can be used for evaluation and what can be used for training. Keep those permissions distinct. Integration & handoff Agree on formats, interfaces and the team that will own the next step. Measurement Set the baseline, comparison set and review process before making a claim about improvement. Practical questions Before we start. Do we need a complete training stack? No. A project can begin with a workflow and an evaluation question. Training infrastructure and integration requirements are scoped separately. Can we start with our existing agent? Yes. The first conversation should cover the agent’s inputs, tools, outputs and known failure modes. We then define the smallest useful evaluation or training deliverable. Which domain do you start with? Accounting is the first working context, through Calibration Arena. The company’s focus is professional knowledge work; other domains require their own expert review and project scope. What results can you promise? A project should commit to specific deliverables and acceptance criteria. Model performance, business impact and deployment readiness must be demonstrated in the engagement; they are not guaranteed by this website. A good place to begin Bring us the work. Let’s make it better. Start with a workflow, a difficult failure, or a standard your agent needs to meet. Discuss a project

One asks whether the entries balance. The other checks the amounts, accounts and dates against the explicit policy. That distinction matters in reinforcement learning. A signal that rewards the easy-to-measure part can miss the behavior the workflow requires. The harder work is deciding what the signal should capture. For a real engagement, the criteria need domain review, difficult counterexamples and a held-out evaluation. This sample illustrates that process; it does not establish a trained model’s performance. company.text: The company The art of better. Calibrated is being built around a simple conviction: agents doing professional work need the standards and practice that make professionals good at it. Observation. Judgment. Repeated refinement. What we are here to do Bring craft to agent training. Craft is a way of paying attention. It means knowing which tolerance matters, recognizing a mistake that looks convincing, and leaving work that another person can pick up. We want those qualities in agents. Our focus is the connection between expert judgment and the material agents learn from: evaluations, reviewed examples, feedback and reinforcement learning environments. We are starting in accounting, where a result can be arithmetically sound and professionally wrong. Calibration Arena is the working tool for that context. Calibrated Co. is the company behind the broader effort. Working principles The habits we bring. 01 Stay close to the practitioner. The person who does the work should help define what good means. Preserve disagreements and the context behind them. 02 Make the standard visible. Explain the task, the criteria and the limits of an evaluation. A result should be possible to inspect. 03 Earn the next claim. Separate a working example from a validated result. Improvement needs a comparison, and a comparison needs evidence. Build with us For people who care how the work is done. We are interested in the intersection of domain expertise, applied research and engineering. If that is where you do your best work, we would like to know what you are thinking about. No open positions are listed here today. You can prepare a collaboration note through our contact page.
